newsitem.title: USA: Lloyd's in talks with rating agencies.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's in talks with rating agencies.

text.p: Lloyd's of London is in talks with the major rating agencies to determine whether a special financal strength rating can be developed for the insurance giant, a top Lloyd's executive said.
Lloyd's will "work in 1997 toward achieving a rating," Lloyd's Chief Executive Ron Sandler told a Coopers & Lybrand Insurance Conference.
However, because Lloyd's is a market of insurance syndicates and not one insurance company, such a move will be complicated, he said.
Agencies such as A.M. Best, Standard and Poor's and Moody's examine the ability of insurance companies to pay claims, and their ratings are crucial in the marketing of insurance.
A claims-paying rating would help to demystify and improve confidence in Lloyd's, Sandler said.
Lloyd's recently completed major restructuring and is in the midst of reviewing its ongoing operations.
A review of Lloyd's regulatory measures was launched about a month ago and is expected to be completed in 1997, he said.
Lloyd's, a self-regulating market, wants to review its practices and learn from the experience of other companies.
Lloyd's also plans to expand its global ooperations in 1997, he said.
Lloyd's has obtained a license to underwrite in Japan and will begin to underwrite in Tokyo next year, he added.
Lloyd's has also being reviewing its operational framework and has decided to keep its current capital security structure and system of global licenses.
He said Lloyd's was not interested in a consolidation of its syndicates into a handful of insurance companies.
"Common security and global licenses are going to stay with Lloyd's for the foreseeable future," he said.
Sandler also said there has been some erosion of confidence in Lloyd's because of its restructuring.
But he said Lloyd's expects 10 to 20 new syndicates to be formed in 1997. This, he said, "demonstrates the vitality of the Lloyd's market.
